findings.title: Dancers cannot build a Shot Kit — the backend requests the nonexistent Claude model `claude-sonnet-5-5`
findings.observed: Every build selects claude-sonnet-5-5 and fails if the provider rejects that model.

findings.title: Dancers can receive kits over their stated budget — build_kit never checks the request's budget against the recomputed cart total
findings.observed: A model cart totaling $12 is returned even when the request specifies a $5 budget.

findings.title: Dancers can receive incomplete or unusable shot plans — model output is silently clamped, dropped or defaulted instead of validated
findings.observed: A single cue, empty filming tip, or out-of-range cue can be returned as a successful kit.

findings.title: Dancers can receive cues for fireworks absent from their cart — cue and cart item IDs are never reconciled
findings.observed: A cue for item 3 and a cart containing only item 6 pass validation.

findings.title: First-time voice users can be recorded after releasing the mic — permission resolution starts the recorder after the release handler has already returned
findings.observed: Releasing before getUserMedia resolves leaves a new recording running with no stop event.

findings.title: Dancers can receive a shot plan with the biggest effect away from the beat drop — the server accepts the model's drop and cue positions without comparing them
findings.observed: An expensive cue at 3s and drop_second 8 are returned unchanged.

findings.title: All visitors lose the stand when the built-in AI key is absent — indexing the environment at import prevents the API server from starting
findings.observed: If EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is absent, importing the server raises KeyError instead of returning 502.

findings.title: Dancers cannot receive generated kits during a database outage — the endpoint makes an unused history insert mandatory and retries the whole model call on insert failure
findings.observed: A completed model response is discarded if shot_kits.insert_one fails.

findings.title: Keyboard users cannot record a voice request — the mic only handles pointer events, not keyboard press and release
findings.observed: Space or Enter on the focused mic fires no recording handler.

findings.title: Dancers cannot copy or share their shot plan with their crew — the kit card has no share or copy action
findings.observed: The generated card offers no copy or share control.

findings.title: Dancers can mistake an old kit for their new request after a failed rebuild — the previous card is kept without its originating request or a stale label
findings.observed: A failed rebuild leaves the previous card visible under the edited request.

findings.title: Catalog visitors see an unexplained empty sheet after a network failure — the only catalog fetch silently ignores errors and never retries
findings.observed: A failed GET /api/catalog leaves the sheet empty without an error or retry.

findings.title: Voice users get a provider error or an empty success for invalid recordings — transcription checks only byte count, not audio type, content or nonempty speech
findings.observed: A nonempty .txt upload is passed to Whisper; an empty provider transcript returns 200.

findings.title: Large audio uploads can exhaust server memory and stall other dancers — the file is read in full before enforcing its size limit
findings.observed: An oversized upload is read fully into memory before the 25 MiB check.

findings.title: Dancers can be stuck indefinitely on Building or Transcribing — neither provider call nor its client request sets a timeout
findings.observed: A stalled model or speech call has no application timeout; the UI remains busy.

findings.title: Dancers see raw provider errors and internal details when a build fails — server exceptions are exposed in the HTTP response and displayed unchanged
findings.observed: The API returns provider exception text and the build toast displays it verbatim.

findings.title: Dancers can fire cues at the wrong moment — the card rounds fractional seconds and marks any cue within 0.6 seconds as the drop
findings.observed: A cue at 7.4s renders 0:07; a cue at 8.5s can be marked as the 8s drop.

findings.title: Blank API requests still trigger paid kit generation — the server length-checks the untrimmed request instead of requiring non-whitespace text
findings.observed: POST /api/shot-kit accepts a request of three spaces and invokes the model.

findings.title: Long voice requests fail with an unreadable validation error — transcription can populate more than 2000 characters and the build handler displays FastAPI's raw detail array
findings.observed: A transcript over 2000 characters yields 422; its validation array is passed to the toast.

findings.title: The stand owner risks uncontrolled provider usage and dancers can lose service to quota exhaustion — public AI endpoints have no rate or concurrency limits
findings.observed: Anonymous callers can invoke the paid transcription and model endpoints without throttling.

findings.title: Dancers can build a kit for their previous request while their new recording is transcribing — mic processing state is not shared with the Build control
findings.observed: Build remains enabled while a new voice transcript is processing, so it can submit old text.

findings.title: Dancers can receive kit instructions in a non-English language — the system prompt and output validation never enforce the chosen English-only language
findings.observed: Model-generated kit names, cues and filming tips are accepted in any language.

findings.title: Phone users can lose part of a song name or filming instruction — unbounded generated words do not wrap inside the clipped kit card
findings.observed: A long unbroken song or cue text extends beyond the card and is clipped by overflow-hidden.

findings.title: Dancers can be left with an active microphone after a recorder error — the error path does not stop the stream acquired before MediaRecorder fails
findings.observed: If MediaRecorder construction or start throws, the already-open stream is never stopped.

findings.title: Dancers can be told a catalog item produces the wrong effect — cue descriptions are trusted from the model rather than checked against the item's effect type
findings.observed: A cue for a Pink Smoke Stick can display an unrelated effect returned by the model.

findings.title: The stand accumulates every dancer's request and kit indefinitely — unused history inserts have no retention or cleanup and eventually consume database capacity
findings.observed: Each generated kit is inserted into shot_kits; there is no read, retention limit or deletion.

findings.title: Dancers can receive a kit for the wrong song or crew — the backend never checks generated song or group details against the request
findings.observed: A kit with song 'B' is returned and displayed even when the request names song 'A'.

findings_minor.title: Dancers can struggle to read unit prices and catalog riel amounts — small slate-500 text falls below the required 4.5:1 contrast
findings_minor.observed: Small slate-500 price text has approximately 4.01:1 contrast on #0D0F1A.

findings_minor.title: Phone users cannot read the full Crew Pack contents in the catalog — its name is forcibly truncated instead of wrapping
findings_minor.observed: The Crew Pack name is truncated in the narrow catalog row with no way to expand it.

findings_minor.title: Dancers see another product's name in the browser tab — the HTML shell retains the template title
findings_minor.observed: The browser tab title is 'Emergent | Fullstack App' instead of BoomDrop.

findings_withdrawn.title: Dancers can leave the microphone recording after leaving the page — the recorder and stream have no unmount cleanup
findings_withdrawn.reason: The single-page source does not establish a reachable React unmount while recording; browser unload itself releases microphone capture.
